_notes: E1 R1.7: the countries a man of the Holy See's diplomatic service may be sent to (docs/EXPANSION-E1-ROME.md §11). Real countries, generated people: the nuncios, secretaries, bishops, and officials he meets are all rolled. Hardship (1..3) and the lines about the Church are invented summaries, flagged; `language` names a credential the game already has, where it has one. `line` is what the post is, shown when the Secretariat offers it (E1 §11.10); invented.

nunciatures.church: a young Church, full on Sunday, short of everything else
nunciatures.line: Nairobi, a nunciature in a garden suburb with a view of the hills, and a conference of bishops that meets more than Rome would like. The work is the seminaries, which are full, and the money, which is not, and a government that is courteous and slow.

nunciatures.church: seminaries that turn men away, and villages where Christians are killed
nunciatures.line: Abuja, a new capital built on nothing, and a nunciature that spends its year on the road. The Church is enormous and the country is dangerous: the dispatches are about kidnapped priests and burned villages, and the bishops are the bravest men you will meet in the service.

nunciatures.country: the Democratic Republic of the Congo
nunciatures.church: the bishops the only national institution anyone trusts
nunciatures.line: Kinshasa, a river the size of a sea, and a nunciature with its own generator. The bishops are the only institution the country trusts, and the government knows it; the nuncio is asked to mediate things nuncios are not meant to mediate. French, and a great deal of patience.

nunciatures.church: two languages, one conference of bishops, and a war in the anglophone west
nunciatures.line: Yaoundé, two languages, one conference, and a war in the anglophone west the capital would rather not discuss. The nunciature is the one place both sides come. The seminaries are full and the roads are bad.

nunciatures.church: growing, orderly, and proud of its schools
nunciatures.line: Accra, a growing, orderly Church proud of its schools, and a government that treats the nunciature as a friend. A good first post: the work is real and nobody is shooting. The bishops will ask you to lunch and mean it.

nunciatures.church: seven rites, a small flock, and the Coptic Orthodox next door
nunciatures.line: Cairo, seven Catholic rites in a city of twenty million, and the Coptic Orthodox next door, who are the Church that matters here. The nunciature's work is the small flock, the schools, and the long conversation with Al-Azhar. French helps; Arabic would help more.

nunciatures.church: the Maronites, the Melkites, the Latins, and a country coming apart
nunciatures.line: Beirut, the Maronites, the Melkites, the Latins, and a state that works in the mornings. The nunciature is on a hill above a city that has been coming apart since before you were born; the patriarchs receive the nuncio, and the secretary waits in anterooms. Hard, and unforgettable.

nunciatures.church: the Chaldeans who stayed, and the ones who are still deciding
nunciatures.line: Baghdad, the Chaldeans who stayed and the ones still deciding, and a nunciature behind blast walls. The work is visas, the Christians of the north, and a government that wants the Church's photograph. A post for a man who can be alone.

nunciatures.church: a Latin patriarchate's parishes, and the refugees from everywhere else
nunciatures.line: Amman, the Latin patriarchate's parishes, the refugees from everywhere else, and a kingdom that likes the Holy See. A quiet post with a great deal of mercy in it: the camps, the schools, the visa lines.

nunciatures.church: a poor Church under a blasphemy law
nunciatures.line: Islamabad, a poor Church under a blasphemy law, and a nunciature that measures its words. The bishops are few and brave; the Christians are the poorest people in the country; the government is polite and watches. The hardest post in Asia, and the one the service remembers you for.

nunciatures.church: three rites, a hundred and seventy dioceses, and a government that counts converts
nunciatures.line: New Delhi, three rites and a hundred and seventy dioceses, and a government that counts converts. The nunciature's year is the ternas, which never end, and the registration office, which never answers. The Church is old, enormous, and quarrelsome, and will feed you.

nunciatures.church: a Church that remembers the Easter bombings
nunciatures.line: Colombo, a Church that remembers the Easter bombings in every parish, and a nunciature on the sea. The work is the aftermath, the government's inquiry, and the Tamil north, where the Church is the only institution left.

nunciatures.church: a small Church with good schools and old missions in the north
nunciatures.line: Bangkok, a small Church with good schools and old missions in the north, and a nunciature that also covers the neighbours. A quiet post in a loud city: the refugees on the Burmese border are the real work.

nunciatures.church: the largest Catholic country in Asia, and a nunciature that is always busy
nunciatures.line: Manila, the largest Catholic country in Asia and a nunciature that is always busy: eighty dioceses, a conference that speaks for the nation, and a politics the Church is inside. Tagalog is a gift here. The work never stops and neither do the typhoons.

nunciatures.church: a minority in the largest Muslim country on earth, strong in the east
nunciatures.line: Jakarta, a Catholic minority in the largest Muslim country on earth, strong in the east, and a nunciature that is careful and respected. Flores and Timor are a Church of their own; the capital is a long conversation about pluralism.

nunciatures.church: a Church founded by laymen, and a border that is still a war
nunciatures.line: Seoul, a Church founded by laymen two hundred years ago and growing still, and a border that is still a war. The nunciature's quieter work is the north, about which it knows more than it says. Korean helps; the bishops speak English.

nunciatures.church: the altiplano's parishes, and a government that argues with the bishops
nunciatures.line: La Paz, the altiplano's parishes at four thousand metres, and a government that argues with the bishops and needs them. The nunciature's work is the Church of the poor and the Church of the city, which are not the same Church. Spanish, and lungs.

nunciatures.church: priests in prison and a government that expels nuncios
nunciatures.line: Managua, priests in prison and a government that expels nuncios: the hardest post in the Americas. The nunciature is watched, the bishops are hunted, and the secretary's dispatches are read in Rome the week they arrive. A post for a man with a long fuse.

nunciatures.church: a peace process the bishops helped broker, and regions it never reached
nunciatures.line: Bogotá, a peace process the bishops helped broker and regions it never reached, and a nunciature that is the busiest in South America. The ternas, the conference, the Amazon's vicariates, and a city that is kinder than its reputation.

nunciatures.church: old cathedrals, new movements, and quarrels between them
nunciatures.line: Lima, old cathedrals, new movements, and the quarrels between them, which reach the nunciature before they reach Rome. The work is the appointments and the movements' files. A good post, with the mountains an hour away.

nunciatures.church: a quiet post, and a good one for learning the work
nunciatures.line: Asunción, a quiet post and a good one for learning the work: a small conference, a government that likes the Church, and a nunciature with a garden and time. The Chaco's missions are the far end of it.

nunciatures.church: a Church that runs the schools and clinics the state cannot
nunciatures.line: Port-au-Prince, a Church that runs the schools and clinics the state cannot, and a nunciature that has been through three earthquakes and two coups. The work is survival and the dispatches are about it. French, and courage.

nunciatures.church: a Greek-Catholic Church under fire, and a Latin one beside it
nunciatures.line: Kyiv, a Greek-Catholic Church under fire and a Latin one beside it, and a nunciature that has not left. The work is the war: the chaplains, the prisoners, the exchanges the Holy See is asked to help with. The hardest post in Europe.

nunciatures.church: Catholics of Polish memory under a government that watches them
nunciatures.line: Minsk, Catholics of Polish memory under a government that watches them, and a nunciature whose telephone is listened to. The bishops are careful and the priests are brave; Polish is the language of half the parishes.

nunciatures.church: a government that wants the Church's photograph
nunciatures.line: Budapest, a government that wants the Church's photograph and a Church that is not sure it wants to be in it. The nunciature's work is the line between them. A comfortable post with a hard question in it; German is useful, Hungarian impossible.

nunciatures.church: full churches, and a concordat nobody wants to reopen
nunciatures.line: Zagreb, full churches and a concordat nobody wants to reopen. A quiet post: the conference is orderly, the government is Catholic in the way that complicates things, and the coast is three hours away.

nunciatures.church: the reports, and what came after them
nunciatures.line: Dublin, the reports and what came after them: a Church that was everything and is now something else, and a nunciature that was once the grandest in Europe and is now a house on a road. The work is listening. A hard post for an Irish-American.

nunciatures.church: cantons, church taxes, and Geneva's international offices next door
nunciatures.line: Bern, cantons, church taxes, and Geneva's international offices next door, where the Holy See has a mission of its own and borrows the nunciature's men. A quiet post with a great deal of paper. German, and the trains run on time.

nunciatures.church: a Royal Commission's recommendations, and the Church still living with them
nunciatures.line: Canberra, a Royal Commission's recommendations and a Church still living with them, and a nunciature in a capital nobody visits. The work is the aftermath, the appointments, and the long distances. A quiet post that is not easy.

nunciatures.church: mission dioceses reached by small planes
nunciatures.line: Port Moresby, mission dioceses reached by small planes, bishops who are also pilots, and a nunciature that covers the Solomons too. The work is distance: a confirmation two days away, a terna gathered by radio. A demanding post, and a holy one.
